model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, retention on standalone equity, subsidiaries added in the bridge

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted equity shares 7,261m = 7,179.8m issued at 2026-09-30 (Q2 FY2027 results) + ~81m dilutive stock options/units (Q2 FY2027 net profit Rs 148,430m / diluted EPS 20.45 = 7,258m weighted diluted, versus / basic EPS 20.68 = 7,177m). Held flat: ESOS/ESUS cost is expensed inside the flow, so option exercises are not also modelled as dilution. Indian banks do not buy back stock.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, standalone Schedule 1A 'Employees stock options/units outstanding': cost recognised during the year Rs 9,687.0m (FY2025 Rs 8,866.2m incl. Rs 964.7m for ICICI Securities options). ESOS/ESUS settle in new shares; there is no net-share-settlement tax line.
inputs.fcf_definition: Bank FCFE, not owner FCF. last_fcf = FY2026 standalone net profit Rs 501,466m (after ESOS cost) less the equity retention needed to fund FY26 net-total-income growth of 8.4% at the FY2026 equity/revenue ratio of 2.839 (2.839 x Rs 91.6bn = Rs 260.1bn) = ~Rs 241.4bn. reported_fcf adds the ESOS cost back (street basis). Actual cash distributed in FY26 was the Rs 78.5bn dividend; the difference is capital the bank accumulated above what growth required. Interest income is the bank's revenue, not an excess-cash return, so interest_income = 0.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:04Z (15:28 IST, final minutes of the NSE regular session; treat as the 13-Nov close)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single INR cost of equity 12.5% in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, through the scenario weights), the same rate used for IBN and HDB so the India private banks compare directly. Built in the flows' own currency: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + beta ~0.85-0.9 x India total equity risk premium ~6.5-7.0% (mature-market premium plus India country premium) = ~12.3-12.6%. This is a cost of equity, not a WACC: the flow is after all funding costs.
inputs.lease_treatment: Bank: rent sits inside operating expenses, i.e. inside profit before tax. No separate lease line; lease_cost_pct_path = 0.
inputs.nci_treatment: Standalone accounts: no minority interest in the flow. The bank's share of subsidiaries is added once, in equity_bridge, as the part of subsidiary profit that does NOT already reach the standalone P&L as dividends.
inputs.notes: MODEL: bank -> dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker'. Run as FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, the house precedent for banks (IBN, HDB, USB, WFC, TFC, NTRS, NAB.AX). IBN is the ADR of this same company (valued 2026-10-04 on the consolidated 20-F at a weighted Rs 943 per equity share); this build uses the STANDALONE Indian GAAP accounts because that is what ICICIBANK.NS_Metrics.csv carries, and adds the subsidiaries in the bridge instead of consolidating them. Engine mapping: revenue = net total income = NII Rs 880,752m + non-interest income Rs 307,576m = Rs 1,188,328m for FY2026 (the CSV 'Revenue' of Rs 2,007,037m is GROSS total income, before interest expense, and is not the base). 'ebitda' = profit before tax Rs 662,184m (after provisions and depreciation) + ESOS cost Rs 9,687m = Rs 671,871m = 56.54% of revenue; sbc 0.815%. da 0 (depreciation is already inside PBT; branch/IT capex Rs 27bn treated as funded within it). Tax 24.3% FY26 effective, 23.7% H1 FY27 -> 24.5% forward. 'capex' = equity retention needed to grow the balance sheet = (equity / revenue) x g/(1+g), with standalone equity Rs 3,373,714m / Rs 1,188,328m = 2.839 at 2026-03-31 (2.86 on Sep-26 equity over TTM revenue). Holding that ratio keeps CET-1 near today's 16.01% against an 8.20% CET-1 minimum (11.70% total); the ~4pp of headroom above any plausible management buffer is NOT released in base or bear and only partly used in bull. FY0 check: (56.54 - 0.815)% x (1 - 0.2427) x 1,188,328 = Rs 501.5bn = reported standalone net profit. net_debt = 0: deposits (Rs 20.5trn) and borrowings (Rs 2.0trn) are operating funding whose interest is already in the flow. ANCHORS (latest filing, Q2 FY2027 results of 2026-10-17, limited review): equity Rs 3,605,935m, BVPS Rs 502.2, GNPA 1.20%, NNPA 0.30%, PCR 75.0%, NIM 4.18%, CET-1 16.01%, contingency provisions Rs 131bn. TTM standalone net profit Rs 546.7bn (diluted EPS 75.4); TTM consolidated Rs 590.7bn. Q2 FY27: PAT +20.1% YoY, NII +17.7%, fees +20.1%, opex +8.5%, provisions Rs 8.5bn. Loans +30.0% YoY / +12.3% QoQ and deposits +27.1% are inflated by FCNR(B) deposit inflows and matching international-branch loans; excluding those, loans +24.1% and deposits +17.0%, and the FCNR(B) book is why NIM fell 18bp QoQ and borrowings rose 62% QoQ. It is treated as low-margin and temporary, not as a new growth rate. No company guidance is given (ICICI Bank does not guide). band_position is not meaningful: ESOS cost is 0.8% of revenue, so house and street differ by a few percent. Qualitative inputs: the filings, IBN_Analysis.json (2026-10-04) and ICICIBANK.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-14, written while this model was being built and checked against it afterwards: NIM compression, CASA slippage, FCNR(B)-inflated growth and CEO continuity to Oct-2028 all match the scenario drivers).

equity_bridge.item: Subsidiaries: bank's share of profit not received as dividends, capitalised at 15x
equity_bridge.note: TTM consolidated profit after minority interest Rs 590.66bn (Q3 FY26 125.38 + Q4 FY26 147.55 + Q1 FY27 154.40 + Q2 FY27 163.33, quarterly press releases) less TTM standalone profit Rs 546.67bn = Rs 43.99bn retained inside ICICI Prudential Life, ICICI Lombard, ICICI Prudential AMC, ICICI Securities, ICICI Home Finance and overseas banks. Dividends the subsidiaries pay up (~Rs 20-25bn a year) are already in standalone other income and are valued in the flow, so only the undistributed part is added. 15x is about the multiple the base case puts on the bank's own earnings; it is deliberately far below market (the listed stakes alone trade at 30x+ earnings), and investments in subsidiaries are carried at cost in the standalone equity used for retention, so nothing is counted twice. Rs 660bn = ~Rs 91 per share.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: bvps_5yr_cagr (FY2021 Rs 213.3 -> FY2026 Rs 471.1 per share, standalone)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (23.9%) starts from the COVID-provisioning year FY2021 and exceeds the equity CAGR (18.0%) by more than 30%: it is a recovery from depressed earnings, not a run-rate. Book value (17-19%) has also grown faster than net total income (13-15%) because payout is only ~16%; equity is accumulating faster than the loan book can use it, which is why ROE slid from 18.6% (FY24) to 15.9% (FY26). The forward model uses 13-14.5% income growth, not the 17% book CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue = net total income (NII + non-interest income), standalone: FY2021 Rs 579.6bn, FY2023 Rs 819.6bn, FY2026 Rs 1,188.3bn. Owner-FCF CAGRs are not computed: a bank's operating cash flow is dominated by deposit, loan and investment flows and is not owner earnings. Source ICICIBANK.NS_Metrics.csv and kpis (INR millions).

base.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 283.9 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income (standalone equity / net total income held at the FY2026 ratio of 2.839, i.e. CET-1 held near 16%).
base.narrative: FY27 net total income grows ~14.5% (H1 FY27 +12.0% against a treasury-gain-heavy H1 FY26; Q2 NII +17.7%, fees +20.1%, loans +24% ex FCNR(B)-backed lending), then fades from 14% to 7% by year 10 and 6.5% nominal INR thereafter. Credit costs normalise from an unusually benign ~0.2-0.3% of loans, taking the pre-tax margin from H1 FY27's ~59.3% of net total income to 56.8% (standalone ROE ~15% on equity held at today's capital intensity). CET-1 is held near 16% - no excess-capital release.

bull.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 265.0 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income (standalone equity / net total income allowed to fall from 2.839 to 2.65: CET-1 drifts from 16.0% toward ~15%).
bull.narrative: India's credit-penetration runway and share gains keep growth at 16-17% for four years; NIM holds ~4.3% once the low-margin FCNR(B) book rolls off, fees compound at ~20%, and opex growing at high single digits against mid-teens income lifts the pre-tax margin to 61.3% (ROE ~17-18%). CET-1 is allowed to drift from 16% toward ~15%, still far above the 8.2% minimum.

bear.capex_rationale: Equity retention = 283.9 x g/(1+g) percent of net total income (standalone equity / net total income held at the FY2026 ratio of 2.839, i.e. CET-1 held near 16%).
bear.narrative: The credit cycle turns after two years of 20-30% corporate and business-banking growth: credit costs rise to ~1% of loans, NIM compresses toward 3.9% under rate cuts and term-deposit competition (average CASA already down to 35.8%), growth slows to 8-11%. Pre-tax margin falls to 49.8%, ROE ~13%, barely above the cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Same 20/50/30 as the IBN valuation of this company. Bear stays above the house 15%: credit costs are at a cyclical low (Q2 FY27 provisions Rs 8.5bn, under 0.2% of loans annualised; GNPA 1.20%) and normalisation is more likely than further improvement, while corporate and business-banking books growing 30%+ YoY is the kind of late-cycle growth that precedes it. The Q1 FY27 uptick in fresh NPA additions that IBN flagged did reverse in Q2 (net additions Rs 12.1bn vs Rs 13.9bn a year earlier), which is why bear is not raised further. Bull 30% (house 35%): it needs above-system growth and margin expansion through an easing cycle.

valuation_philosophy.summary: ICICI Bank is valued as a bank: free cash flow to equity (standalone net profit less the equity that must be retained to fund balance-sheet growth at today's capital ratio) discounted at a 12.5% INR cost of equity, with deposits and borrowings treated as operating funding (net debt = 0) and the subsidiaries added once for the profit they retain. The judgment that matters is ROE against cost of equity against growth: at ~15-16% ROE and 13-14% growth roughly 85% of earnings must be retained, so near-term FCFE is thin and value rests on the long growth runway and the terminal. The model's terminal implies about 10x earnings and 1.5x book in year 10; the stock has not traded below ~1.5x book in the past decade and sits near the top of its 1.5-3.2x range today, so the gap to the market price is mostly a disagreement about the discount rate and how long a premium multiple persists, not about the next two years of earnings.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit-cost normalisation: provisions are running at Rs 35-55bn a year on an Rs 18trn loan book; a return to 1% of loans is ~7-8pp of pre-tax margin, the bulk of the bear case.
NIM: 4.18% in Q2 FY27 after an 18bp drop from FCNR(B) inflows; average CASA ratio down to 35.8%. Rate cuts reprice loans faster than term deposits.
Cost of equity and terminal growth in INR: this is long-duration value; one point on the discount rate moves the base case by roughly a fifth (see the sensitivity grid).
Excess capital: CET-1 16.0% against an 8.2% minimum is held, not released. A higher payout or faster deployment would add value that is not in base.
Subsidiaries are in at 15x retained profit (~Rs 91/share); at market value of the listed stakes the figure would be two to three times that.
Standalone basis: figures are Indian GAAP standalone; the IBN (ADR) valuation of the same company uses the consolidated 20-F, so per-share values differ slightly by construction.
Regulatory: RBI group-structure directions and subsidiary ownership rules; the additional agricultural priority-sector provision (Rs 12.8bn) pending RBI review.
